author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Hikers planning a White Mountains outing this weekend face sharply different conditions from one day to the next, with slick trails and powerful summit winds Friday followed by a much calmer Saturday.

The Mount Washington Observatory’s recreational forecast said muddy surfaces will linger through Friday. Temperatures at higher elevations may fall below freezing early, while patchy summit fog reduces visibility. A wind chill advisory for the higher summits remains in effect until 10 p.m., and northwest gusts above hurricane force are possible in the morning. Valley and notch gusts could reach 30 mph.

Saturday is expected to bring the best window for longer trips. Sunshine, warmer air and light winds are forecast across elevations. The observatory advised hikers to carry enough water and sun protection despite the cooler start to the weekend.

Sunday should stay warm and mostly dry for much of the day, but moderate west winds and summit fog are expected to return at higher elevations. Clouds will increase, with a chance of showers and isolated thunder Sunday afternoon. A lightweight rain layer remains a sensible addition even for outings that begin under favorable skies.
dek: A rough Friday above treeline is forecast to give way to sunshine, warmer temperatures and lighter winds across New Hampshire’s mountains.
headline: Saturday brings a better White Mountains hiking window
